Parameterized explainer (PGExplainer)

Source: R/explain-pg-subgraphx.R
pg_explainer.Rd

PGExplainer (Luo et al. 2020) learns one small network that predicts an edge mask for any instance from the model's node embeddings, instead of optimizing a separate mask per instance as gnn_explainer() does. For an edge \(u \to v\) the mask logit is \(\omega_{uv} = \mathrm{MLP}([z_u, z_v, z_t])\) for a node target \(t\) (or \([z_u, z_v]\) for a graph level output), with \(z\) the trained model's last hidden representation (return_embedding = TRUE), which is not updated.

Usage

pg_explainer(
  model,
  data,
  targets = NULL,
  hidden = 64L,
  epochs = 30L,
  lr = 0.003,
  edge_size = 0.05,
  entropy = 1,
  temperature = c(5, 2),
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'pg_explainer'
predict(object, g, target = NULL, ...)

Arguments

model

A trained model or graph_fit that accepts return_embedding = TRUE (for example from gnn_model()).

data

A graph_data object (node level models) or a list of them (graph level models).

targets

For node level models, the target nodes to train on (default: training nodes, at most 100).

hidden

MLP hidden size.

epochs

Passes over the instances.

lr

Learning rate.

edge_size, entropy

Mask size and entropy penalties.

temperature

Start and end temperature of the concrete relaxation.

seed

Optional integer seed.

object

A pg_explainer.

g

Graph to explain.

target

Target node (node level models), or NULL.

...

Unused.

Value

pg_explainer(): an object of class pg_explainer; predict(explainer, g, target): a graph_explanation whose edges table holds the mask probabilities.

Details

Training samples a relaxed Bernoulli (concrete) mask \(m = \sigma((\log \epsilon - \log(1 - \epsilon) + \omega) / \tau)\), \(\epsilon \sim U(0, 1)\), multiplies it into edge_weight, and minimizes the negative log probability of the class the model predicts on the full graph (squared change for one output regression), plus edge_size times the mask sum and entropy times the mask entropy. The temperature \(\tau\) decays geometrically from temperature[1] to temperature[2]. The fitted explainer then explains a new instance with one forward pass, \(m = \sigma(\omega)\).

Like gnn_explainer(), the mask acts through edge_weight, so the model must use edge weights; the explanation shows how the model responds to edges, not causal relevance.

References

Luo et al. (2020) Parameterized explainer for graph neural network. NeurIPS.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  g <- split_nodes(dataset_karate(), seed = 1)
  fit <- train_graph_model(gnn_model("gcn", 34, 8, 2), g,
                           "node_classification", epochs = 20, seed = 1)
  pg <- pg_explainer(fit, g, epochs = 3, seed = 1)
  ex <- predict(pg, g, target = 1)
  head(ex$edges[order(-ex$edges$attribution), ])
}
#>    edge from to attribution
#> 68   68   13  4  0.01817265
#> 67   67    4 13  0.01761832
#> 20   20   12  1  0.01725827
#> 66   66    8  4  0.01619467
#> 65   65    4  8  0.01572598
#> 70   70   14  4  0.01511737
